sources.title: D1 dopamine receptors in prefrontal cortex: involvement in working memory
sources.used_for: Foundation: D1R blockade in monkey dlPFC selectively impairs memory-guided saccades (not visually-guided)
sources.notes: Seminal paper establishing D1R role in WM maintenance phase

sources.title: Modulation of memory fields by dopamine D1 receptors in prefrontal cortex
sources.used_for: D1 antagonists potentiate memory fields in single-unit PFC recordings

sources.authors: Zahrt J, Taylor JR, Mathew RG, Arnsten AF
sources.title: Supranormal stimulation of D1 dopamine receptors in the rodent prefrontal cortex impairs spatial working memory performance
sources.used_for: Establishing right-side of inverted-U: D1 agonist SKF81297 impairs WM in dose-dependent manner

sources.title: Decreased prefrontal dopamine D1 receptors in schizophrenia revealed by PET
sources.used_for: Human PET evidence: reduced D1R binding in dlPFC of SCZ patients, correlated with negative symptoms and WCST performance
sources.notes: Abstract only; subsequent PET studies show mixed findings

sources.authors: Goldman-Rakic PS, Castner SA, Svensson TH, Siever LJ, Williams GV
sources.title: Targeting the dopamine D1 receptor in schizophrenia: insights for cognitive dysfunction
sources.used_for: D1R dysfunction → cognitive deficits in SCZ; D1 enhancement as therapeutic target

sources.authors: Vijayraghavan S, Wang M, Birnbaum SG, Williams GV, Arnsten AF
sources.title: Inverted-U dopamine D1 receptor actions on prefrontal neurons engaged in working memory
sources.used_for: Key cellular mechanism: low D1R → sharpen tuning (suppress non-preferred); high D1R → suppress all firing. cAMP-mediated.
sources.notes: Behaving monkey, single-unit recording during WM task

sources.authors: Paspalas CD, Wang M, Arnsten AF
sources.title: Constellation of HCN channels and cAMP regulating proteins in dendritic spines of the primate prefrontal cortex: potential substrate for working memory deficits in schizophrenia
sources.used_for: Immunoelectron microscopy: D1R and HCN2 channels co-localize in dendritic spines of layer III dlPFC. cAMP signalplex.

sources.authors: Gamo NJ, Lur G, Higley MJ, Wang M, Paspalas CD, Vijayraghavan S, Yang Y, Ramos BP, Peng K, Kata A, Boven L, Lin F, Roman L, Lee D, Arnsten AF
sources.title: Stress Impairs Prefrontal Cortical Function via D1 Dopamine Receptor Interactions With Hyperpolarization-Activated Cyclic Nucleotide-Gated Channels
sources.used_for: Causal proof: D1R activation → HCN channel opening → WM impairment; ZD7288 (HCN blocker) reverses impairment and stress-induced cognitive deficit
sources.notes: Multi-species (rat, monkey, mouse); behavioral + electrophysiological evidence

sources.authors: Arnsten AF, Girgis RR, Gray DL, Mailman RB
sources.title: Novel Dopamine Therapeutics for Cognitive Deficits in Schizophrenia
sources.used_for: D1 inverted-U and therapeutic implications for SCZ cognitive deficits

sources.authors: Arnsten AF, Wang M, Paspalas CD
sources.title: Dopamine's Actions in Primate Prefrontal Cortex: Challenges for Treating Cognitive Disorders
sources.used_for: D1R vs D2R anatomical segregation: D1 on layer III spines (Delay cells), D2 on layer V dendrites (Response cells)

sources.authors: Weber MA, Conlon MM, Stutt HR, Wendt L, Ten Eyck P, Narayanan NS
sources.title: Quantifying the inverted U: A meta-analysis of prefrontal dopamine, D1 receptors, and working memory
sources.used_for: 75-study meta-analysis; inverted-U best fit; D1R alone explains 26% of WM variance vs 10% for general dopamine

sources.authors: Cumming P, Abi-Dargham A, Gründer G
sources.title: Molecular imaging of schizophrenia: Neurochemical findings in a heterogeneous and evolving disorder
sources.used_for: Review of D1R PET findings in SCZ, noting mixed findings (some studies show elevated frontal D1R in relation to cognitive deficits)
sources.notes: Abstract only; important for noting contested nature of D1R-SCZ PET findings

sources.authors: Alamo C, López-Muñoz F, Sánchez-García J
sources.title: Mechanism of action of guanfacine: a postsynaptic differential approach to the treatment of ADHD
sources.used_for: Guanfacine mechanism: α2A-AR → inhibit cAMP → close HCN channels; opposite of D1R excess. ADHD treatment rationale.
sources.notes: Spanish journal; used for mechanistic overview only

sources.title: Prefrontal dopamine and behavioral flexibility: shifting from an 'inverted-U' toward a family of functions
sources.used_for: Inverted-U may not apply uniformly to all PFC cognitive functions (set-shifting, decision-making may differ)
sources.notes: Used for the 'controversy' section - inverted-U generality debate

sources_summary.notes: ≥5 sources, ≥2 open full texts (PMC), ≥1 official institution (NIH-funded Arnsten lab). Minimum criteria met.
